steps.title: Record the fork settings
steps.instruction: Count the rebound clicks (top) and compression clicks (bottom) from fully in, and note the fork leg height in the clamps.
verification: Clicker counts and fork height recorded.

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand so the front wheel is off the ground and the bike cannot tip.
verification: Front wheel off the ground, bike stable.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts, remove the axle nut, pull the axle and drop the wheel out, guiding the disc out of the caliper. Take the collars off the hub. Do not pull the brake lever with the wheel out.
verification: Front wheel out, collars kept.

steps.title: Move the brake aside
steps.instruction: Remove the number plate. Remove the front brake hose holder bolts and the two caliper bolts and hang the caliper clear with the hose still connected.
verification: Caliper hanging clear, hose not stretched.

steps.title: Remove the fork legs
steps.instruction: Support each leg. Remove the fork protector. Loosen the upper pinch bolts, loosen the fork cap (damper assembly) with a cap bolt ring wrench, loosen the lower pinch bolts and slide the leg out. Repeat for the other side.
verification: Both legs out, caps loosened.

steps.title: Unscrew the cap and drain
steps.instruction: Unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, slide the outer tube down and pour the outer-chamber oil out into a pan.
verification: Outer chamber drained.

steps.title: Release the bottom adjuster
steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and set the cap bolt ring wrench between the inner tube and the locknut. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster from the bottom of the leg. Never remove the locknut: the damper rod can drop into the damper and be lost.
verification: Adjuster off, locknut still on the rod.

steps.title: Take out the damper and spring
steps.instruction: Remove the cap bolt ring wrench, lift the damper assembly out with the fork spring and spring seat, and take the damper adjusting rod out.
verification: Damper, spring and rod out.

steps.title: Separate the tubes
steps.instruction: Prise off the dust seal and remove the seal retaining clip with a flat screwdriver without scratching the tube. Push the inner tube in slowly to just before it bottoms, then pull it back sharply; repeat until the tubes separate. Slide off the piston metal, slide metal, washer and oil seal.
verification: Tubes apart, bushings and seal off.

steps.title: Remove the base valve
steps.instruction: Record the compression setting, then hold the damper with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench. Drain the damper oil.
verification: Base valve out, damper drained.

steps.title: Inspect fork parts
steps.instruction: Inner tube: scratches can be cleaned with #1000 wet paper; a damaged oil lock piece or deep scoring means replacement. Inner tube bend limit 0.2 mm (0.01 in) (half the dial reading); never straighten a bent tube. Outer tube: scratches, wear or damage means replacement. Fork spring free length: standard 497.0 mm, limit 492.0 mm (19.37 in). Damper assembly: bends or damage; O-rings worn. Base valve: wear, damage, contamination; base valve bushing and spring; bleed screw. Upper spring seat contact face. Adjuster O-ring.
verification: All fork parts inspected; measurements recorded.

steps.title: Fill and bleed the damper
steps.instruction: Stretch the damper fully and fill it with 216 cm³ (7.30 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1. Pump the rod slowly up and down with about a 200 mm (7.9 in) stroke to bleed it; longer strokes pull air in (then start again). With the damper fully stretched, the oil level must be 145–148 mm (5.71–5.83 in) below its top.
verification: Damper oil level measured at 145-148 mm.

steps.title: Fit the base valve
steps.instruction: Finger-tighten the locknut fully onto the damper rod. Fully loosen the compression adjuster (record its setting first). Pull the damper rod out to build pressure, then screw the base valve in while letting the rod back. The damper must sit fully stretched; if not, start the fill again. Tighten the base valve to 28 N·m (21 lb·ft).
verification: Base valve 28 N·m; damper fully stretched.

steps.title: Settle the damper oil
steps.instruction: Pump the damper slowly more than 10 times. Wrap it in a cloth, compress it fully and let the excess oil (about 10 cm³) overflow out of the base valve side hole. It must move smoothly with no tight spots; if not, repeat the fill.
verification: Damper moves smoothly after overflow.

steps.title: Fit new seals and bushings to the inner tube
steps.instruction: Oil the inner tube. Slide on a new dust seal, the seal retaining clip, a new oil seal (numbered side down, over a plastic sleeve with fork oil to protect the lip), the washer and a new slide metal. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips with lithium-soap grease. Fit a new piston metal into the inner tube slot.
verification: New seal, slide metal and piston metal on.

steps.title: Join the tubes and drive the seal
steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube on. Drive the slide metal and washer home with the fork seal driver, then drive the oil seal in until the clip groove is fully visible. Fit the retaining clip fully into its groove, then the dust seal. The tubes must slide smoothly.
verification: Seal seated, clip in groove, tubes slide smoothly.

steps.title: Set the locknut height
steps.instruction: The distance from the bottom of the damper assembly to the bottom of the locknut must be at least 16 mm (0.63 in); turn the locknut to correct it.
verification: Locknut distance measured, 16 mm or more.

steps.title: Fit spring and damper
steps.instruction: Fit the spring seat (larger end toward the spring) and the fork spring on the damper. Let the damper slide slowly down the inner tube until it reaches the bottom; do not drop it.
verification: Damper and spring in place.

steps.title: Refit the bottom adjuster
steps.instruction: Record and fully loosen the rebound adjuster. Fit the damper adjusting rod, a new copper washer and the adjuster, compress the inner tube and set the cap bolt ring wrench under the locknut, and finger-tighten the adjuster onto the damper. The gap between adjuster and locknut must be 0.5–1.0 mm (0.02–0.04 in). Hold the locknut and tighten the adjuster to 29 N·m (21 lb·ft). Then fit the adjuster into the inner tube with threadlocker at 55 N·m (41 lb·ft).
verification: Gap 0.5-1.0 mm; 29 N·m; 55 N·m with threadlocker.

steps.title: Fill the outer chamber
steps.instruction: Pour in 290 cm³ (9.80 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (allowed range 260–365 cm³). Screw the damper assembly into the outer tube hand-tight and fit the protector guide.
verification: Outer chamber filled with the recorded quantity.

steps.title: Do the other leg the same
steps.instruction: Repeat the bench steps on the other leg. Both legs must have the same oil quantities; uneven legs make the bike unstable.
verification: Both legs serviced with equal oil.

steps.title: Refit the forks
steps.instruction: Slide each leg in to its original height (standard: top of the outer tube 0 mm (flush) above the upper clamp) and snug the lower pinch bolts. Tighten the fork cap to 30 N·m (22 lb·ft) with the ring wrench. Tighten the upper and lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft); do not over-tighten the lower ones, the fork will bind. Refit the protectors at 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft).
verification: Caps 30 N·m; pinch bolts 21 N·m; protectors torqued.

steps.title: Refit the caliper and number plate
steps.instruction: Refit the caliper at 28 N·m (21 lb·ft), the brake hose holder bolts at 9 N·m (6.6 lb·ft) and the number plate at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
verification: Caliper 28 N·m; holders 9 N·m.

steps.title: Refit the front wheel
steps.instruction: Fit the collars, guide the disc between the pads and push the axle (greased with lithium-soap grease) through. Tighten the axle nut to 112 N·m (83 lb·ft). Before tightening the pinch bolts, push hard on the bars several times so the forks settle, then tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Axle nut 112 N·m; pinch bolts 21 N·m.

steps.title: Pump up the front brake
steps.instruction: Pull the front brake lever until it is firm and check the wheel spins freely without the brake dragging.
verification: Lever firm, wheel free.

steps.title: Restore the clickers
steps.instruction: Turn each damping adjuster in finger-tight and back out to the recorded setting.
verification: Clickers back to the recorded settings.

completeness: Covers front wheel, front end strip, stem removal, bearing and race check and renewal, greasing, ring nut preload, stem nut, clamps and refit.

required_parts.name: Steering bearings (2) with races
required_parts.purpose: Renewed as sets when pitted or damaged.

critical_stop_conditions: Head tube bore damaged by a race: stop.
Steering tight or notchy after tightening: back off the ring nut a little; do not ride with binding steering.
Bent or cracked bracket or stem: replace.

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand so the front wheel is off the ground and the bike cannot tip.
verification: Front wheel off the ground, bike stable.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.instruction: Loosen the four axle pinch bolts, remove the axle nut, pull the axle and drop the wheel out, guiding the disc out of the caliper. Take the collars off the hub. Do not pull the brake lever with the wheel out.
verification: Front wheel out, collars kept.

steps.title: Strip the front end
steps.instruction: Remove the number plate and front fender (four bolts). Remove the brake hose holder bolts and the caliper and hang them clear. Remove the lower handlebar holder nuts and lift the handlebar off with its controls. Loosen the steering stem nut. Support and remove both fork legs (loosen upper and lower pinch bolts).
verification: Front end stripped to the clamps.

steps.title: Remove the stem
steps.instruction: Remove the steering stem nut and the upper bracket, then the washer. Support the lower bracket and remove the steering ring nut with a steering nut wrench, then lower the stem out.
verification: Lower bracket and stem out.

steps.title: Check bearings and races
steps.instruction: Wash the bearings and races in solvent. Pitting or damage on a bearing or race means bearing and race are replaced as a set. Check both brackets and the stem for bends or cracks.
verification: Bearings, races and brackets checked.

branches.label: Bearings and races good
branches.condition: Both bearings and all races are free of pitting and damage.

steps.title: Renew bearings and races
steps.instruction: Drive the old races out of the head tube with a long rod and hammer, working round evenly. Remove the race from the lower bracket with a chisel. Fit the new races squarely; a crooked race damages the head tube.
verification: New races seated square.

steps.title: Grease and fit the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Fit the lower bearing on the stem with lithium-soap grease on the dust seal lip and the bearing inner circumference.
verification: Lower bearing greased and fitted.

steps.title: Fit the upper bearing
steps.instruction: Fit the greased upper bearing and the bearing race cover, greasing the cover lip.
verification: Upper bearing and cover in.

steps.title: Fit the stem and ring nut
steps.instruction: Grease the stem threads and bearing seats and push the stem up. Fit the steering ring nut with its stepped side down. With the steering nut wrench tighten it to about 38 N·m (28 lb·ft), loosen it one full turn, then retighten it to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Turn the stem lock to lock: it must move smoothly; if it binds, take it apart and check the bearings.
verification: Ring nut: 38 N·m, back one turn, 7 N·m; stem turns freely.

steps.title: Refit washer, forks and upper bracket
steps.instruction: Fit the washer, the fork legs and the upper bracket. Set the forks to the recorded height (standard: top of the outer tube 0 mm (flush) above the upper clamp) and snug the lower pinch bolts.
verification: Forks at height, lower pinch bolts snug.

steps.title: Tighten the stem nut
steps.instruction: Grease the stem nut contact face with lithium-soap grease and tighten the nut to 145 N·m (107 lb·ft). Check the steering still turns smoothly; if it is tight, back the ring nut off a little at a time.
verification: Stem nut 145 N·m; steering smooth.

steps.title: Tighten the clamps
steps.instruction: Tighten the upper and lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft); do not over-tighten the lower ones.
verification: Pinch bolts 21 N·m.

steps.title: Refit bars, brake and fender
steps.instruction: Refit the handlebar with its holders the way they came off and tighten the lower holder nuts to 40 N·m (30 lb·ft). Refit the caliper at 28 N·m (21 lb·ft), the brake hose holders at 9 N·m (6.6 lb·ft), the front fender at 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft) and the number plate at 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
verification: Holders 40, caliper 28, hose holders 9, fender 10, plate 7 N·m.

steps.title: Refit the front wheel
steps.instruction: Fit the collars, guide the disc between the pads and push the axle (greased with lithium-soap grease) through. Tighten the axle nut to 112 N·m (83 lb·ft). Before tightening the pinch bolts, push hard on the bars several times so the forks settle, then tighten the four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
verification: Axle nut 112 N·m; pinch bolts 21 N·m.

steps.title: Pump up the front brake
steps.instruction: Pull the front brake lever until it is firm and check the wheel spins freely without the brake dragging.
verification: Lever firm, wheel free.

steps.title: Check for play
steps.instruction: With the front wheel off the ground, rock the fork legs back and forth: no play. Turn the bars lock to lock: no binding and no cable or hose snagging.
verification: No play, no binding.

steps.title: Free the chain
steps.instruction: Remove the chain joint clip and joint and take the chain off.

steps.title: Remove the linkage

verification: Relay arm and connecting arm off.

steps.title: Remove the swingarm
steps.instruction: Remove the pivot shaft nut and pull the pivot shaft, then lift the swingarm out.

steps.title: Renew the linkage bearings

steps.title: Fit the swingarm

verification: Pivot nut torqued.

steps.title: Fit the linkage

steps.title: Check the travel

verification: Smooth travel.

steps.title: Refit chain, brake and pedal

Press the brake pedal until firm.
verification: Slack in range; axle and locknuts torqued; brake firm.

steps.instruction: Remove the collars, washers and seals from the relay arm and connecting arm and press out the needle bearings by their outer race. Press new bearings in flush (0 mm) and fit the washers and new seals flush (0 mm).
verification: Linkage bearings and seals flush.

steps.title: Grease everything
steps.instruction: Pack the bearings, thrust bearings, bushings, collars, washers, seal lips and the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease. Grease the linkage and shock bolts (shank and thread).
verification: All bearings and bolts greased.

steps.title: Fit the swingarm
steps.instruction: Fit the swingarm and push the pivot shaft in from the right. Tighten the pivot nut to 75 N·m (55 lb·ft), with lithium-soap grease on the nut threads and face.
verification: Pivot nut torqued.

steps.title: Fit the linkage
steps.instruction: Fit the connecting arm bolt on the frame side from the right; fit the connecting arm bolt on the relay arm side, the relay arm bolt on the swingarm side and the shock lower bolt from the left. Tighten: connecting arm nut frame side 80 N·m (59 lb·ft), connecting arm nut relay arm side 80 N·m (59 lb·ft), relay arm nut swingarm side 70 N·m (52 lb·ft), shock lower nut 53 N·m (39 lb·ft).
verification: Linkage 80/80/70 N·m; shock lower 53 N·m.

steps.title: Check the travel
steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm through its full travel by hand: smooth, no binding or knock.
verification: Smooth travel.

steps.title: Refit chain, brake and pedal
steps.instruction: Fit the chain with its joint and a clip whose closed end faces the direction of chain travel. Slide the caliper bracket back onto the swingarm rail and refit the hose in its guides. Refit the brake pedal spring and bolt at 26 N·m (19 lb·ft).
verification: Chain clip correct; pedal bolt 26 N·m.

steps.title: Refit the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Fit the collars, wheel (disc between the pads), left chain puller, greased axle from the left, right puller, washer and nut. Set chain slack to 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with equal adjustment and the wheel pushed forward. Tighten the axle nut to 135 N·m (100 lb·ft) and the adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Press the brake pedal until firm.
verification: Slack in range; axle and locknuts torqued; brake firm.
